plan.gap_statement: The model assumes cytosolic calcium extrusion remains first-order over all amplitudes, omitting pump saturation at elevated cytosolic calcium.
plan.baseline_assumption: Calcium extrusion is represented by a nonnegative first-order rate constant k_extrusion multiplying C for all cytosolic calcium levels.
plan.scientific_mechanism: Finite-capacity ATP-dependent calcium pumps and exchangers produce saturable clearance, making net calcium removal sublinear at higher cytosolic calcium.
plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax the idealized linear-extrusion assumption rather than add a new compartment or pathway. Vary stimulus_strength while holding the initial conditions, k_release, k_sensor_activation, and k_sensor_relaxation fixed. In the parent, once H is specified, the target mapping dC_dt versus C has constant negative slope from extrusion, so stronger stimulation mainly rescales how far release initially exceeds a linear sink. In the child, the sink slope decreases as C enters the pump-saturation regime, creating extra curvature in the target mapping itself, not merely in the auxiliary H trajectory. This yields a concrete observable contrast: under weak stimulus both models can look similar because C stays in the low-occupancy regime, but under stronger stimulus the child predicts disproportionately larger peaks, slower high-C decay, or higher sustained calcium before inhibition catches up. A single refit of the parent parameters cannot reproduce both low-amplitude near-linear damping and high-amplitude reduced incremental clearance across those conditions, because its removal term has one fixed slope in C at all amplitudes. The refinement remains scientifically admissible so long as calcium stays nonnegative and the saturating pump law is chosen to preserve nonnegative removal.

plan.activation_condition: Observable when stimulus_strength is large enough that C rises into a regime where reversible endogenous binding would load appreciably during the transient, and on observation windows comparable to buffer binding/unbinding times rather than infinitely fast quasi-equilibrium buffering.
plan.train_hidden_contrast: In training, the mechanism appears as weaker early-time slope and lower peak during strong calcium transients; in holdout or longer trajectories it extends to a slower post-peak decay because buffer unloading sustains free calcium after release has been curtailed.

plan.promotion_reason: History-dependent sequestration cannot be represented by refitting only existing fixed coefficients because the parent maps dC_dt from the current C and H alone. plan.baseline_assumption: Calcium buffering is absorbed into effective rates and is not modeled as a separate state.
plan.scientific_mechanism: Finite-capacity reversible binding of cytosolic calcium to endogenous buffers that transiently sequester free calcium and later release it.
plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax the effective-rate treatment of buffering and add explicit reversible buffer occupancy. The parent target mapping has a fixed-environment shortcut: once C and H are specified, dC_dt is fully determined by a release term opposed by extrusion, so prior calcium loading history cannot matter. Scientifically, many calcium transients are shaped by endogenous buffers whose occupancy changes over time. Vary stimulus_strength while holding all kinetic parameters and initial conditions fixed: under sufficiently strong stimulation, the child should show a reduced initial rise and lower peak free calcium because newly available buffer binds calcium, plus a more prolonged decay after release subsides because bound calcium is returned. The parent can mimic some peak reduction by refitting release or extrusion gains, but one shared parameter set cannot simultaneously create both stronger transient attenuation during the upswing and delayed tail support at matched C and H, because it lacks a hidden occupancy variable. This contrast is observable only when buffering loads appreciably over the sampled C range and on timescales not collapsed into an instantaneous algebraic renormalization. If buffering is weak or effectively instantaneous with negligible occupancy variation, the refinement reduces back toward the parent.

Vary stimulus_strength while holding all other parameters and initial conditions fixed. In the parent, stronger stimuli mainly scale the amplitude and duration of C excursions, and H accumulation follows proportionally because dH_dt has no activation curvature beyond the (1-H) occupancy factor. In a child with cooperative or saturating calcium dependence of sensor activation, small calcium excursions generated under weaker stimulus produce noticeably less H buildup than predicted by the parent, whereas moderate excursions generated under stronger stimulus cross into a steeper activation range and suppress release sooner. This changes the scored mapping indirectly but consequentially through H, because the observed dC_dt at the same C and H trajectory history now comes from a differently curved H evolution that feeds back onto release. The contrast is scientifically admissible when calcium pulses reach the sensor's activation range; if C stays uniformly tiny or uniformly very high, the refinement becomes hard to distinguish. A single refitted parent parameter set cannot generally match both weak-response underactivation and moderate-response sharp feedback onset across those conditions, because changing k_sensor_activation only rescales one linear slope instead of introducing the needed curvature.

response_change.parent_relation: The inhibitory sensor activates with a linear calcium dependence k_sensor_activation*C*(1-H), so at fixed H the suppression pathway strength grows with a single low-calcium slope and no intrinsic activation threshold curvature.
response_change.child_relation: Replace the linear calcium dependence of sensor activation by a steeper saturating calcium dependence so that inhibition accumulates weakly at very low C and disproportionately faster once C reaches a moderate activation range.
response_change.observable_effect: Across fixed stimulus_strength with identical initial conditions, low-amplitude calcium elevations produce less inhibition buildup than in the parent, while moderate elevations trigger earlier and stronger delayed suppression, changing pulse width and the onset of oscillation termination.

contract.activation_condition: Observable when C traverses a low-to-moderate range during transients or oscillations, so that sensor activation is neither always near zero nor always fully saturated; especially when stimulus_strength is large enough for CICR to lift C into this regime but clearance and inactivation still terminate excursions.
contract.train_hidden_contrast: In training, the same mechanism changes how H accumulates during ordinary calcium pulses; in holdout, the contrast extends to stronger pulses where the steeper activation curvature produces earlier shutdown and altered oscillation envelopes.
contract.continuation_path: The parent law is recovered in the limit where the refined sensor-activation nonlinearity reduces to linear dependence on C over the sampled range.
contract.domain_mechanism: Nonlinear calcium occupancy of the inhibitory sensor
contract.scientific_mechanism: Cooperative calcium binding or multistep occupancy in the inhibitory sensor, causing nonlinear accumulation of the active inhibitory fraction as calcium rises.
contract.difficulty_rationale: This embedding is harder than a coefficient-only correction because the effective activation coefficient of the inhibitory pathway now depends on the evolving state C, introducing response curvature that a single constant k_sensor_activation cannot reproduce across weak and moderate pulses.
contract.assumption_before: Sensor activation rate is linear in free calcium concentration with one fixed slope and no intrinsic curvature or threshold-like occupancy effect.
contract.assumption_after: The inhibitory sensor has saturating calcium-dependent occupancy, so its activation coefficient depends on the current calcium level.
contract.before_fragment: (k_release*stimulus_strength*(1 - H))/(1 + release_inactivation_scale*C) + (k_cicr_release*stimulus_strength*C*(1 - H))/(1 + release_inactivation_scale*C) - (k_extrusion*C)/(1 + pump_saturation_scale*C) - (k_buffer_bind*C*(1 - B))/(1 + buffer_binding_scale*C) + k_buffer_unbind*B
contract.after_fragment: (k_release*stimulus_strength*(1 - H))/(1 + release_inactivation_scale*C) + (k_cicr_release*stimulus_strength*C*(1 - H))/(1 + release_inactivation_scale*C) - (k_extrusion*C)/(1 + pump_saturation_scale*C) - (k_buffer_bind*C*(1 - B))/(1 + buffer_binding_scale*C) + k_buffer_unbind*B
contract.parent_reduction: The parent is recovered exactly when sensor_activation_scale = 0, or approximately when sensor_activation_scale*C << 1 throughout the sampled trajectories.
contract.observable_signature: Vary stimulus_strength while holding all other parameters and initial conditions fixed. Under weaker stimuli that keep C low, H accumulates less than in the parent; under stronger stimuli that lift C into the moderate activation range, H builds more abruptly and shuts release down earlier. This altered H trajectory feeds back onto the release terms and changes the scored dC_dt mapping across conditions through delayed inhibition, not merely an auxiliary unobserved branch.
contract.shortcut_blocked: A single refitted parent parameter set can only rescale the linear activation slope k_sensor_activation in dH_dt. That cannot simultaneously match weak-response underactivation and moderate-response sharper feedback onset across the stated conditions, because the child introduces calcium-dependent curvature in the inhibitory-loading law rather than a uniform gain change.

range_suggestions.sensor_activation_scale: positive; chosen so sensor_activation_scale*C is small at resting calcium but can become order one during ordinary pulses, allowing weak low-C activation and stronger curvature at moderate C
